topic: HashAgent: Share an AI Agent as a URL That Runs Locally via WebGPU

key_points: Runs production-ready LLMs directly in the browser via WebGPU with near-native performance
100% private, zero server costs, offline-capable after initial model download
Switches between MLC, Transformers.js, Flare, and Demucs engines; supports structured output, TTS, speech recognition, and audio source separation
SDK + no-code builder (Browseragent.dev); ~1.4k GitHub stars
Focus is on dev library + no-code agents, not a shareable-URL protocol
Privacy-first AI chat (ThinkHere) that runs entirely in the browser via WebLLM + Transformers.js + WebGPU
Two runtimes: WebLLM+MLC (precompiled WebGPU shaders) and Transformers.js+ONNX (wider model range, WASM fallback)
Multimodal input (Gemma 4 image/audio), local RAG knowledge base with embeddings stored in IndexedDB
Models cached after first download; no servers or API keys
Chat-focused, not an agent-shareable-URL system
First web-native AI agent harness built on browser primitives: Workers, origins, sandboxing, OPFS, WASM/WASI, WebRTC, WebAuthn, WebExtensions
Runs fully inside Chrome/Firefox, can read and drive tabs, signed-in sessions, web apps
Supports hosted models, localhost local models, and preliminary local WebGPU/WebNN support
No peerd account or hosted browser required; Apache 2.0
Different approach: harness pulled into the browser (browser-native agent runtime) rather than a URL-shareable focused agent
High-performance in-browser LLM inference engine (18.5k stars) — the underlying engine HashAgent uses
Ahead-of-time compiled models via Apache TVM into optimized WebGPU compute shaders
prebuiltAppConfig model registry that HashAgent checks against
Enables fast local inference with smaller download sizes
Run Hugging Face Transformers directly in the browser with no server (16.2k stars) — second engine HashAgent uses
ONNX Runtime Web backend, WASM fallback when WebGPU unavailable
Supports a wider range of architectures; verified ONNX community exports used for models like Gemma 4, Qwen3.5, LFM2
ONNX Runtime Web WebGPU EP not supported on iOS browsers — a key constraint

stats.fact: HashAgent compresses an agent's behavior + runtime profile into one URL via deflate-raw + URL-safe base64 (#agent= payload)
Requires current Chrome/Edge 113+ or Safari 26+ on hardware with WebGPU; ONNX WebGPU EP unsupported on iOS, so iPhones stay on WebLLM
Built-in models range from SmolLM2 360M (~210MB download, ~580MB runtime memory) up to Llama 3.1 8B (~4.3GB download, ~5.0GB runtime)
Auto profile uses SmolLM2 360M on phones and Qwen2.5 3B on desktop-class devices (~1.66GB download, ~2.5GB runtime)
Protocol v2 separates agent behavior from the runtime model — a phone does not blindly honor an 8B model hint; profiles: auto | mobile | balanced | quality | vision
No inference server, no account, no tracking, no analytics code, no cookies; chat ephemeral by default with optional IndexedDB persistence; agent payload never sent in HTTP requests
Optional stateless Cloudflare Pages Functions gateway (/api/search, /api/read) because search providers and arbitrary public pages block direct browser CORS; can be disabled
Underlying engines: WebLLM ~18.5k GitHub stars, Transformers.js ~16.2k stars; GPUWeb spec repo ~5.4k stars
HashAgent launched on Hacker News Aug 14 2026 (story 49298088) — 38 points, 4 comments, front-page
HN community noted browser models are relatively tiny (only small models fit in-browser) but praised making local AI accessible

angles: Privacy-first: entire agent (definition + inference + storage) runs on-device — no inference server, account, or tracking — the strongest differentiator vs cloud agents
Shareable-by-URL agent protocol: a full agent's behavior and runtime profile compressed into one self-contained hash URL; device picks a safe model from the profile
Honest device-model matching: protocol v2 prevents a phone from blindly loading an 8B model; memory budgets and download sizes are surfaced to the user before any download
Local-first tools: weather (Open-Meteo) and Wikipedia fetched directly from the browser; optional gateway only for search/read that browsers block via CORS
The practical ceiling: browser-fit models are relatively tiny (360M–8B) — trade-off of local execution vs capability; iOS/ONNX constraints
WebGPU as the enabler: two mature engines (WebLLM + Transformers.js) now make truly local inference viable, with real memory/download economics
Build-your-own fork: fully open source, gateway can be disabled, no telemetry — fits the self-host/sovereignty crowd
